ns1:channel.ns1:title: Communications Earth & Environment
ns1:channel.ns1:description:
Communications Earth & Environment is an open access journal from Nature Portfolio that publishes high-quality research, reviews and commentary in the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. The papers we publish represent significant advances that bring new insight to a specialized area of research. We also provide a community forum for issues of importance to Earth, environmental and planetary scientists, regardless of sub-discipline.

Our scope covers all areas of the geosciences, climate and environmental sciences as well as planetary sciences, including those at the interface with ecology, sustainability and environmental social sciences. Primary research of interest to the journal includes important insights gained from field work, novel analyses of existing data, numerical or analytical modelling, theoretical studies or laboratory experiments.

We encourage submissions that provide independent confirmation of particularly influential publications.

The submission and review processes are managed by our in-house professional editors supported by our Editorial Board Members, who provide technical expertise across the breadth of the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. We are committed to rapid dissemination of important research results. Articles are published on a continuous basis to ensure swift communication of findings.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Long-lived replenishment of magmas in the oceanic upper mantle revealed by chromite nodules in ophiolites
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04015-8

Chromite nodules grow through Ostwald ripening over timescales of 10⁴ to 10⁶ years, recording prolonged magma replenishment and slow cooling in the oceanic upper mantle, according to combined microstructural observations and Monte Carlo Potts modeling of chromite nodule formation in ophiolites.
ns1:item.dc:title: Long-lived replenishment of magmas in the oceanic upper mantle revealed by chromite nodules in ophiolites

Paul T. Robinson

ns1:item.ns1:title: Reduced BVOC emissions from birch forest understory during coupled insect outbreak and microclimatic forcing
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04057-y

Severe moth outbreaks in Swedish birch forests reduced volatile compound emissions from understory vegetation by 38-70%, likely due to both direct herbivory and changes in understory microclimate following mountain birch defoliation, based on two years of field measurements

ns1:item.ns1:title: Peatlands mapped across the European Alps with a harmonised multi-sensor workflow show widespread degradation
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04036-3

Degraded and unmapped Alpine peatlands can be identified to prioritize monitoring and restoration across borders, based on a multi-sensor workflow combining Sentinel satellite and terrain data validated against 590 peatlands in the European Alps.
ns1:item.dc:title: Peatlands mapped across the European Alps with a harmonised multi-sensor workflow show widespread degradation

ns1:item.ns1:title: Nutrient stress reduces the extent but increases the intensity of root-driven destabilization of mineral-associated organic matter
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04008-7

Under resource limitation, shifts in rhizodeposition enhance destabilization intensity of mineral-associated organic matter, whereas in nutrient-rich soils, higher root growth drives the overall extent of destabilization, based on isotope tracing and metabolomics.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Clean-air regulation reduces childhood wasting and overweight in China
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 15 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04061-2

In China, the rollout of clean-air regulation has reduced both wasting and overweight in early childhood, according to analyses of county-level health and pollution data.
